thread.title: Research Analysts’ Updated EPS Estimates for July, 6th (AAPL, ALV, BDSI, BIG, CHKP, DG, DLTR, ERJ, FME, FRE)

author: ABMN Staff
title: Research Analysts’ Updated EPS Estimates for July, 6th (AAPL, ALV, BDSI, BIG, CHKP, DG, DLTR, ERJ, FME, FRE)
text:
Research Analysts’ updated eps estimates for Friday, July 6th:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) had its price target raised by Loop Capital from $195.00 to $210.00. Loop Capital currently has a buy rating on the stock. Get Apple Inc alerts:
Autoliv (NYSE:ALV) was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a strong-buy rating. They currently have $115.00 price target on the stock. According to Zacks, “On Jul 1, 2018 Autoliv has closed the spin-off of its electronics segment, Veoneer, Inc. This spin-off completes the process is in line with its strategy to establish its electronics segment as a separate entity. The underlying aim was to create two isolated entities, capable of catering to two different markets, with separate product offerings. For full-year 2018, Autoliv has provided a positive outlook for its Passive Safety business while estimating negative growth for its other business, i.e. Electronics Systems. It is undertaking innovative product launches, acquisitions and JVs, which are likely to boost sales. In order to boost shareholder confidence, the company actively pursues capital deployment strategies.”
BioDelivery Sciences International (NASDAQ:BDSI) had its buy rating reaffirmed by analysts at HC Wainwright. They currently have a $3.50 price target on the stock. The analysts wrote, “Valuation and risks. We assume Belbuca continues to grow rapidly to $125M by 2022 (approximately $150M peak), with BDSI cash- flow positive in 2020, and fully profitable by 2021. Our $3.50 12- month price target is based on a DCF with an 11% WACC discount, and negative -15% terminal growth beyond 2027.””
Citigroup Inc initiated coverage on shares of Big Lots (NYSE:BIG) . Citigroup Inc issued a buy rating on the stock.
Check Point Software Technologies (NASDAQ:CHKP) was upgraded by analysts at OTR Global to a positive rating.
Citigroup Inc began coverage on shares of Dollar General (NYSE:DG) . Citigroup Inc issued a buy rating on the stock.
Citigroup Inc assumed coverage on shares of Dollar Tree (NASDAQ:DLTR) . The firm issued a neutral rating on the stock.
Embraer (NYSE:ERJ) had its hold rating reiterated by analysts at William Blair.
Fresenius Medical Care AG & Co. KGaA (ETR:FME) was given a €102.00 ($118.60) target price by analysts at Nord/LB. The firm currently has a buy rating on the stock.
Fresenius SE & Co KGaA (FRA:FRE) was given a €82.00 ($95.35) target price by analysts at Nord/LB. The firm currently has a buy rating on the stock.
Citigroup Inc initiated coverage on shares of Kroger (NYSE:KR) . They issued a buy rating on the stock.
LKQ (NASDAQ:LKQ) was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a strong-buy rating. The firm currently has $37.00 price target on the stock. According to Zacks, “LKQ Corp. has been growing its footprint through organic expansion and acquisitions. In May 2017, the company completed the acquisition of German-based Stahlgruber, thus, strengthening its position in Europe. Further, the company is lowering its operational costs by changing the pay for sales reps from commission basis to a more customer-centric basis. Also, its focus on the aftermarket defends the company from cyclical nature of the automotive industry. Over the past year, LKQ Corp. has outperformed the industry it belongs to.”
Lululemon Athletica (NASDAQ:LULU) had its price target boosted by Bank of America Corp from $121.00 to $140.00. Bank of America Corp currently has a buy rating on the stock.
MarketAxess (NASDAQ:MKTX) was downgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a sell rating. According to Zacks, “MarketAxess Holdings’ shares have underperformed the growth of its industry in the past year. The company has also witnessed its Zacks Consensus Estimates move downward over the past 90 days. The valuation of the shares look stretched at the moment. Escalating costs remain a headwind for the company for quite some time. The margins are getting affected by the increase in total expenses over the last few years. Moreover, given the ongoing investments of the company in several areas, the same is going to rise in the upcoming quarters as well. The company is also exposed to foreign exchange volatility risk. However, growth strategy such as acquisitions and alliances, and consistent increase in commission received on trading volumes are reasons behind its revenue growth. Its solid inorganic growth is also a positive on the back of a strong financial position.”
Marvell Technology Group (NASDAQ:MRVL) had its target price trimmed by UBS Group AG from $38.00 to $33.00. They currently have a buy rating on the stock.
Citigroup Inc started coverage on shares of Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage (NYSE:NGVC) . Citigroup Inc issued a buy rating on the stock.
Nokia Oyj (NYSE:NOK) was downgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a sell rating. According to Zacks, “Nokia has considerable operations in geographies outside the United States. Presently, when the economy in Europe is highly unpredictable post the Brexit referendum, it becomes difficult for the company to increase revenues and reduce costs. In addition, Nokia is likely to be stifled by the renegotiated deals and restrictions imposed on trade with other European Union members. Brexit could further result in higher tariff and non-tariff barriers to trade between the U.K. and the European Union, lowering its productivity. The company’s trailing 12-month return on equity undercuts its growth potential. Continued below-par performance of Nokia’s Networks unit remains a concern. The stock has also underperformed the industry in the past year on an average. However, Nokia is continuously expanding its businesses into targeted, high-growth and high-margin vertical markets to improve its bottom line in the long term.”
PepsiCo (NASDAQ:PEP) was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a sell rating to a hold rating. According to Zacks, “PepsiCo’s shares have outperformed the industry in the past month as investors recognize its efforts to boost top line. PepsiCo is witnessing strong performances in its international divisions, driven by higher revenue growth in the developing and emerging markets. The company is also gaining from its solid brand portfolio, product innovation and strong snacks business. Notably, the company has delivered positive earnings surprise for eight consecutive quarters. However, the consumers’ awareness on health and wellness, alongside new taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages and growing regulatory pressures are affecting CSD sales. Notably, the company’s NAB division reported dismal results with revenues and operating profit decreasing 1% and 22%, respectively, in first-quarter 2018. Volumes declined 2.5%, led by 4% decline in CSDs and 1% decrease in Non CSDs. Estimates have been going down ahead of second quarter earnings.”
Pool (NASDAQ:POOL) was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a buy rating. They currently have $169.00 price target on the stock. According to Zacks, “Pool shares have outperformed the industry in the past year. In fact, first-quarter 2018 marked the 31st consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth for Pool in sales. Notably, the company should continue to benefit in the near term backed by base business sales growth and favorable trends in the housing market. Additionally, continuous growth in the remodel and replacement sectors of its business is a major positive. The company’s leading market share position and opportunistic expansion strategies position it well for revenue growth. Nonetheless, seasonality of the company’s business and macroeconomic headwinds owing to large global presence raise concern. Earnings Estimate have remained stable over the past two months.”
Penn Virginia (NASDAQ:PVAC) had its target price raised by LADENBURG THALM/SH SH from $100.00 to $110.00. The firm currently has a buy rating on the stock.
Royal Dutch Shell plc ADR Class A (NYSE:RDS.A) was downgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a strong-buy rating to a hold rating. According to Zacks, “Shell’s shares have risen +30% in the past one year, outperforming the Zacks Integrated Oil industry's +21% increase. The performance is backed by impressive earnings suprise history. Shell’s $50 billion buyout of BG Group has boosted its strong and diversified portfolio of global energy businesses that offers attractive long-term growth opportunities. It has also made Shell the largest LNG producer which would help the company meet the fuel’s growing demand and boost cash flows. Importantly, the aggressive divestment plans of Shell have streamlined its production and helped in debt reduction. However, at same time the divestment spree has affected the volumes growth. With the production going down as evidenced in the last few quarters, the near-to-medium term outlook remains cloudy. Hence, we advise investors to wait for a better entry point before buying shares.”
Royal Dutch Shell plc ADR Class A (NYSE:RDS.A) was upgraded by analysts at DZ Bank AG from a hold rating to a buy rating.
Regulus Therapeutics (NASDAQ:RGLS) had its price target lowered by B. Riley from $1.00 to $0.50. The firm currently has a neutral rating on the stock.
William Blair started coverage on shares of Re/Max (NYSE:RMAX) . William Blair issued an outperform rating on the stock.
Starbucks (NASDAQ:SBUX) was upgraded by analysts at DZ Bank AG from a sell rating to a hold rating. They currently have $48.00 price target on the stock, down from their previous price target of $52.00.
Citigroup Inc started coverage on shares of Sprouts Farmers Market (NASDAQ:SFM) . They issued a buy rating on the stock.
Citigroup Inc initiated coverage on shares of Smart & Final Stores (NYSE:SFS) . Citigroup Inc issued a neutral rating on the stock.
